title: Directional Message Passing for Molecular Graphs
layout_note: A narrow 'Model:' column at the left (RBF and SBF basis thumbnails feeding an Embedding block and a stack of Interaction blocks summed into t) is followed by four tinted detail panels titled in bold with a colon: Embedding (green) and Residual (pink) stacked, a wide Interaction panel (blue) with a nested pale 'Directional message passing' sub-box, and Output (tan).
grouping: Each block type has one fill colour used both for its boxes in the model stack and for the background of its detail panel: green Embedding, blue Interaction, pink Residual, tan Output. Panel titles are bold serif text with a colon placed above the panel's top-left corner. Inside the Interaction panel a lighter blue inset box groups the directional message-passing operations.
shapes_depth: Flat rectangles with thin black outlines, no rounding or shadows. Layer boxes contain their equation (sigma(W box + b), W box) rather than names, using an empty square as the input placeholder. Operators are white circles with symbols (concatenation ||, Hadamard dot, sum over k or j, plus). Two small embedded plots (radial basis curves, spherical basis heat-map) sit at the top of the Model column as input thumbnails. Lines are thin black orthogonal arrows; inputs are bold italic math with superscripts (e_RBF^(ji), m_kj^(l-1)).
proposed_highlight: The directional message passing, the contribution, is the only nested inset (pale blue box with its own label) inside the largest panel, and the Interaction panel occupies about a third of the width; the SBF angular basis thumbnail at the top of the Model column shows the directional input.
lesson: Writing each layer as its formula inside the box (sigma(W box + b), with a square as the input slot) lets detail panels show exact computation with no separate equations, and colour-matching each block type between the model stack and its panel removes zoom lines.
notes: Venue from the first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2020'). The Output block appears as a small tan box at the end of the Embedding and Interaction panels, so the per-layer outputs t_i^(l) leave each panel at the right edge and are summed in the Model column.

arrangement.units: Five regions in a row: an untinted 'Model:' column (basis thumbnails, embedding + 6 interaction boxes, a sum circle), then tinted rectangular panels with bold colon titles: Embedding (green) above Residual (pink), Interaction (blue, widest, with a pale inset for directional message passing), Output (tan).
arrangement.inputs_as: bold italic math symbols (distances, angles, basis vectors, messages) with arrows entering each panel from the top; two small basis-function plots in the Model column
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the target t leaves the sum circle at the right of the Model column
arrangement.shared: Output and Residual blocks are drawn as small coloured boxes inside other panels and expanded once in their own panel; inputs e_RBF and a_SBF reappear as text labels at the top of each panel rather than linked lines

taxonomy.task: molecular property prediction with directional (angle-aware) message passing

core.what: a narrow overview column on the left (RBF/SBF bases, Embedding, a stack of Interaction blocks, a sum) opened into detail panels tied by matching tint, the blue Interaction panel the widest with a nested pale inset for directional message passing

relations.form: the overview's green Embedding block and blue Interaction blocks are expanded into green and blue panels to the right, and a pink Residual and an orange Output panel unpack the blocks reused inside them
overview column top to bottom: Embedding, six Interaction blocks, each emitting an output to the right into one summation node producing t
in the Interaction panel the incoming message m_kj and the SBF basis are combined through W-projections, an element-wise product and a bilinear layer, summed over k, then added to m_ji
the RBF and SBF bases are drawn as small plots of the radial curves and the spherical pattern at the top of the overview

channels.colour: panel tint = block type, matching the overview: green = Embedding, blue = Interaction, pink = Residual, orange = Output; the pale-blue inset marks the directional message-passing core
channels.shape: white rectangle = a layer (W, sigma(W+b), Embedding); circle = an operation (product, concat, sum, plus)
channels.line: solid arrows only; inputs enter from the panel tops as long vertical lines
channels.frame: tinted panel = one block type; the nested inset = the contribution

quality.strengths: Each block is taught once in its own tinted panel and reused compactly by tint (Residual and Output appear as pink and orange boxes inside other panels); the contribution gets the largest panel and the only nested inset; the bases are drawn as plots.
quality.weaknesses: Several long parallel input lines down the Interaction panel's left edge cross the inset border and run to the bottom Output box, so which input feeds which operation is hard to trace; layers carry formulas (sigma(W□+b), □^T W□) rather than names; the overview's tinted blocks are not linked to the panels by callouts, only by tint.

insights.structure: A narrow model column at the left (basis inputs, embedding, a stack of interaction blocks, a sum) is followed by four colour-tinted detail panels, the Interaction panel the widest and holding a lighter inset for the directional message-passing core.
insights.data: Inputs are bold italic math with superscripts entering from panel tops, plus two small basis-function thumbnails (radial curves, spherical heat-map) feeding the model column; every layer box shows its formula with an empty square as the input slot.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the only nested inset in the figure, a pale-blue labelled box inside the largest blue panel.
insights.flow: Each panel reads top to bottom with thin orthogonal arrows, while per-block outputs exit right through small tan Output boxes toward the Model column's sum circle.
insights.avoid: The Interaction panel has several long parallel input lines on its left edge running down to its bottom Output box, crossing the inset's border and making it hard to tell which input feeds which operation.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
